column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, one clause: Trajan allowed Prusa's bath only if it left no less for necessary spending in the years ahead, the plan's order in one ruler's sentence (payments bought first, IPS l.11-l.15), read in Latin at source; it competes with Carnegie (Q167-001, Q167-009) for the one outside name in its part; say the plan's order, since the extra Treasuries are the report's answer, never inside IPS l.13 (Q167-016).

Thu 19 Nov: store and a true fact behind the word pencil: Prusa's bath was to be paid from debts Pliny had only begun to collect, money counted before it was in hand, as Laura names no figure before its Treasuries are held (NUMBERS 4); idea 3's pattern; never a new conceit turn.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; Pliny's first audit and Trajan's accounts first are the building's work, and facility costs are outside the case (l.164); no decision served.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-025 (owned money removes only the money reason a building stalls): adds only the edition conflict; fix Q167-025's sum to more than three million sesterces, since the Latin Library text reads 3,318,000 and Firth 3,329,000.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; Trajan's collusion is a cause among public officials, and Laura polices no one; colour.

Thu 19 Nov: store, pedigree for every number says where it came from: Pliny gave Nicaea's sum with why it was unsure (the accounts not made out), as 3d gives $95,000 held since January 2028 and the rest since January 2031 (SKELETON 3d, checked); no new decision.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-023: the Nicaea donors' promises were postponed, already in its quote; the pairing with Kresge's 2008 more time, not refunds (Q51-004, SD-7) travels with it; her co-sponsors' pledges lapse after December 2032, which Nicaea's did not.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or SD-7, one clause at most: Pliny's warning against spending more to save money already spent, about AD 112; Laura's figure is held, not spent, until 2033, so her money never faces his choice before then; a vivid early statement, never the first; the timing is the case's, so fit 2; if the building slips past January 2033 her money waits in short-term Treasuries (SD-7's weakness).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-031 (her top comes from what she owns, not the building's need): Trajan's content with a sufficient gymnasium was a ruler's cap on a city, and the critic was a rival.

Thu 19 Nov: store and a true fact behind ink and pencil: Pliny kept fees paid apart from fees still to be demanded, as Laura's words keep her own $115,000 apart from the pledges and never add them (SD-1); never the conceit in her spoken words (CONCEIT V2.2).
Thu 19 Nov: store only; decisions left to those at the building is known and serves no part; facility costs are outside the case (l.164).
Thu 19 Nov: store, colour behind Q167-025's limit: works begun before checking failed on engineering and religion, not money.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d wording guard, and a correction: Trajan read every promise toward a building as made for the building, so her figure is unconditional only of markets and of the co-sponsors' pledges, never of the building itself; fix Q167-023's mapping and the aha register's Nicaea reserve (first and without conditions) to that scope; round 9's either way sentence already fits; a building never built stays SKELETON 3d's open item.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-023 (donors' named parts waited on the core): adds that Nicaea's pledges were works, not sums; the naming-rights prediction is Keel inference, UNVERIFIED, store only.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; idle Roman money is colour beside NUMBERS 3's short-term Treasury ETF; say paid even if cash waiting earns nothing (WORDS), never met.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; a city's claim on private debtors with its rank unsettled against her claims on the Treasury; held for her, never identified (Q157); no part needs it.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; a gift building nobody kept up is colour, not a decision of the plan; her payments are a base for running the residency, never its whole budget (H9-119).

Thu 19 Nov: store only; fix the idea column: by its own critique Dio oversaw public money and was not the giver, so say an overseer's accounts were checked; his identification is unchecked; the comfort letter (Q99) carries the showing of holdings.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: at Sinope Pliny tested the ground cheaply and gathered the money before asking, and Trajan allowed it only if the city could bear it alone, the reverse of Nicaea and the money half of Laura's order (NUMBERS 4); modico impendio is Keel's translation; testing the ground stays the residency's job.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q180-019: the Nicaea and Sinope pair is row 19 beside Q167-023; the letters' order shows a change, not its cause.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-021 (reliance binds): Trajan let a twenty-year grant stand to protect those who relied on it; the half-kept mapping fails, since Piso received the grant and did not give it.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-021: Trajan's nothing changed in the past is non-retroactivity for laws and prizes, not pledges; a known rule; never as raising or cutting a stated range (3b).
Thu 19 Nov: store only, beside IPS l.9: Pliny built with his own money while bad harvests cut his rents; land can be sold and a career cannot, which is the IPS's point; colour.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 store, row 25's companion: Pliny's gifts to Comum carried their own upkeep money (CIL V 5262, Radice via livius.org; Latin unread); his upkeep was interest on capital, so never call her reserve an endowment, and her payments are a base for running the residency, never its whole budget (H9-119).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3d lead-in, one clause with row 1: the same man gave buildings with their upkeep and, as governor, saw cities stall on money spent before checking or counted before collecting; competes with Q167-009 (Carnegie) for the one outside name; gift dates unchecked, so claim only both sides, never that Bithynia taught him.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, SD-3's evidence clause, and a correction: Nicaea went first by spending, and the money sank, so Laura goes first by owning and holding until 2033, never by spending; Q167-023's mapping (the work which had to be finished first, in money) and the aha register's Nicaea reserve need this fix; date it about AD 112, since the letters carry no year.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-007 (no, yes, no): FASB's October 1982 draft is the first no; adds dates and letter counts; fixes Q173 idea 1's tried it for thirteen years and gave it up to a thirteen-year exception between two noes.
Thu 19 Nov: store: the 1983 majority said yes because paying early in cash was not always feasible, and Laura cannot pay a residency that does not yet run; pedigree only, no decision of the plan.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-001 (the 1983 rule): para 27 is the reasoning behind para 3(c); its IPS l.11 mapping is row 10's risk half and Q173 idea 1(b); her set-aside is not irrevocable.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-014 (the rule flattered the books): written at the request of those it flattered overreads, since the text gives no motives.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a verbs, one clause: the 1983 dissent's own words (for a debt to be satisfied, the creditor must be satisfied), read at source, are the primary line for why a payment is met only when the residency is paid; supersedes Q173-017's critic's summary as the line to quote.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e pedigree and a correction: the 1983 rule names a failure of the trust's own cash flows (a Treasury default) and a lender's acceleration, which no one can do to Laura; a missed deposit is the set-aside never completed, on neither list; fix Q173-012's reason 1 mapping, Q173-013 and its rater's fix: a Treasury default is the one named case, never both of IPS l.17's reasons.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.2, a standard-setter behind Book 19's risk-free: FASB drew the line between Treasuries and top-rated company bonds, not between bonds and shares; say risk-free of the Treasuries, never of a fund's payout; the iBond funds pass the reason, not the letter (Q173-003's fix); footnote 3 read in part.
Thu 19 Nov: store, Figure 1 pedigree: the 1996 board barred netting set-aside assets against a liability, as Figure 1 shows each payment beside its Treasury; already the design.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a pedigree and a correction of Q173 idea 1(a): FASB says the 1996 reversal changed the test from risks and rewards to control, so never say it found set-aside Treasuries unsafe; Book 19's words for them stand.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, one clause behind the definition: ink's two halves match accounting's two tests, will pay it on its date the 1983 risk test and owned the 1996 control test, so ink is never paid; sharpens Q173-003 and Q173 idea 2; the T-bonds pass the 1983 letter, the iBond funds only its reason; bond syntheses tested as pedigree (aha test 8), so cold-test it before calling it an aha.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, the card's strongest: in 1985 FASB ruled that bonds bought to pay on a pension's dates reduce risk but settle nothing because the investment decision can be reversed, Laura's ladder exactly, read at source; say the ten Treasuries, dedicated portfolio once at most in 2.5 (WORDS); never only two things can break the plan (Q109-033).

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q186-011: para 28 is the same ruling with its mortality reason, and her ten fixed $50,000 payments have no lifespan to guess (as H2-110); fix: the first $39,162 is needed if cash waiting earns nothing (NUMBERS 8u).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e, one sentence: FASB's three tests applied to her give no, no and yes from January 2028, so what they leave is her own decision, which IPS l.17 names; fix: never the one soft spot, since fund costs past the margin, an early fund end at zero interest (NUMBERS 3) and custody delay (Q72) are hers too; gives Q3b-033 (a policy, not a law) a standard-setter's tests.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c pedigree, one clause: the pension rule counts a settlement only once done, and the probability of completion is not relevant, as Laura states her range only after the move (certain after the move, NUMBERS 4); the parallel is the order, not the instrument.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q186-011: EY's undedicated at any time is FAS 88's can be reversed in a firm's words; its 3e point is Q3b-033's.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-012 (the same 1996 list): adds item (e), no lender party to the trust, which the Codification marks superseded; its mapping (no one signed for her Treasuries) is Q54-042's legal shell.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q186-009: the 1996 reasons that apply to her ask whose money it is, never whether it pays; $46,566 and $75,934 checked (NUMBERS 8h), said as worth about $46,600 in 1 January 2033 money if rates hold (WORDS); reason (d) is already Q173-012's.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-011: the Codification's matter of law adds nothing a report needs.

Thu 19 Nov: store only; fix: the 2021 change took probable out of when an obligation counts, not out of how sure a payment is, so never cite it for 3c's certain; Q173-005 carries that point; the FAS 76 link is Keel's.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-027 with its fix: the IPS calls the commitment fixed and non-negotiable (l.11) and the case calls the ten commitments, so never say the ten are avoidable at her discretion or not yet a debt.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d or 3c: accounting's test for when a promise binds (others justified in relying: its recipients, a credible promise, harm if it fails) puts reliance at the 2031 meetings; the relation is Q167-021's and Q18-014's, so one of the three at most, this one for a finance judge; co-sponsors receive her statement, not her money (Q147-001).

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q186-014: the join of rows 14 and 21; Q173-023 holds the bond-law form of the same order; say accounting agrees with the order, never that it is why the IPS moves first (l.15's reason is money she already owns).

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-011: the verbs (set aside, already in Treasuries she owns, met only on each payment date) are WORDS's and Q173-011's; never already met, settled, defeased or sufficiently met for the ten.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q186-008: the 1983 rule's continuing disclosures are Figure 1's display point again.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q20-023: a date fix only, GASB 7 is March 1987, filling Q173's gap.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-008 (the opposite motive): gains and window dressing, from an abstract; Laura books no gain.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-016: swaps are not defeasances and the lesson overreads the same way; never as evidence of how co-sponsors judge her figure.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q173-016 as its citation guard: cite the 1990 abstract (a reliably negative stock reaction), never the 2010 summary.

Thu 19 Nov: store: New Zealand's rule reinstated a defeased debt once its assets ceased to be risk-free, so a set-aside holds only while it is kept, as hers holds by IPS l.17; one of Q15-006 and this at most; never cannot move; AASB 1014 unread.
